intent: Materialize S19 Memory Governance and S20 Temporal Task Governance together over S18 while preserving one memory graph/replay and one S6 scheduler.
falsifications_that_changed_design: Root-only forget is insufficient: unsupported derived cognitive state must be invalidated while alternate current support survives.
A scheduled intent cannot be copied as plaintext into task and wake journals when S26+ privacy/backup/erase are considered.
A failed schedule authorization can otherwise leave an orphan plaintext capsule.
A forget tombstone bound to only the originating runtime session can be lost after future restore/migration.
A governance wrapper is insufficient if the local product still starts TemporalAutonomyRunner directly; the canonical poller must be governed.
runtime_chain: S19 preview-forget -> exact ACTION_CONFIRMATION -> append-only governance tombstone -> support-aware temporal closure -> replay reconciliation
S20 governed schedule -> one erasable intent capsule + opaque S6 token -> exact S6 schedule -> task binding -> current memory/capsule validation -> governed wake -> fresh authority barrier
local product -> GovernedTemporalTaskRunner -> governed S6 poll only

future_pressure.S21: intent/plan reconciliation consumes S19/S20 envelopes but may not bypass them
future_pressure.S22: external assist receives no implicit memory/task authority
future_pressure.S23: connectors require fresh scope at use time
future_pressure.S25: resident/native host may not become a second cognitive runtime
future_pressure.S26_plus: backup/update/migration must preserve tombstone precedence, capsule retention/erase semantics and schema fail-closed behavior

commit_chain.semantic: subordinate product temporal polling to governance

claim_boundary: All mutation counts are modeled architecture/fault-vocabulary cases. They are not production reliability estimates and are not one million physical crashes, browser runs, connector calls, transactions or native-host executions.
